name: pdk-dbt-pinterest-dbt
instr:
We switched most tables of our Pinterest Ads connector to Fivetran history mode, mainly so the URL report can credit each day to the URL a pin had that day. Since then the package's reports in /app are wrong: spend and conversions are too high, and some campaign, ad group and pin names and statuses are old ones. A sample of what the connector writes now is in /data/pinterest_ads/, one CSV per source table, shaped like the seeds in /app/integration_tests/seeds plus Fivetran's system columns.

Every report should count each report row once, at the numbers Pinterest has for it now, and leave out report rows deleted in Pinterest. Names, statuses and other details should be the ones each advertiser, campaign, ad group, pin and keyword has now; ones deleted in Pinterest keep the last details they had. In pinterest_ads__url_report and pinterest_ads__pin_promotion_report, the destination URL and the fields parsed from it should be the ones the pin had at the end of that day, UTC. Tables that aren't in history mode should give the same results as before, apart from leaving out deleted report rows.

The reports keep their columns and grain. dbt seed and dbt build in /app/integration_tests have to pass on the new tables and on the project's own seeds with its data tests, and rebuilding after the next sync has to match a fresh build. The project stays SQL: only SQL models, macros and YAML, with no Python models. There's no network; dbt-duckdb and the project's packages are installed, and
